report:
### Conclusion
Current scientific evidence indicates that while hypnotherapy may assist some individuals in quitting smoking, there is no strong evidence showing it is consistently effective or superior to standard, evidence-based smoking cessation methods.

### Key Evidence
* **Cochrane Review Findings:** A comprehensive systematic review of randomized controlled trials evaluated hypnotherapy for smoking cessation and concluded that there is insufficient evidence to show it leads to higher long-term quit rates than other behavioral interventions or brief support.
* **National Institutes of Health (NIH):** The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH) notes that although hypnosis is one of the most studied complementary approaches for quitting smoking, scientific evidence regarding its efficacy remains inconclusive.
* **Clinical Application:** Organizations like the Mayo Clinic suggest that hypnosis may be useful for some patients as a component of a comprehensive treatment plan to address behavioral habits and cravings, but it is generally recommended alongside or secondary to first-line therapies (such as counseling and nicotine replacement therapy).

### Sources
* Cochrane Evidence: https://www.cochrane.org/th/evidence/CD001008_does-hypnotherapy-help-people-who-are-trying-stop-smoking
* PubMed Central (Cochrane Review Text): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6568235
* National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NIH): https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/providers/digest/complementary-health-approaches-for-smoking-cessation-science
* Mayo Clinic: https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/hypnosis/about/pac-20394405
